doc: Degenerate input: back = -p (the first four points, exact negation) with f = 0.5 gives a zero vector, which normalizes to NaN (0 / 0 in IEEE, numpy warning suppressed); the last two points are ordinary. NaN equals NaN in the comparison; documents what the oracle does, a caller never passes an exactly antipodal back (the flow moves a point at most ~1 rad). Arguments: p and back (inputs, direction vectors of shape (..., 3)) and f (params): q = normalize(p (1 - f) + back f), with normalize(v) = v / ||v|| over the last axis (sphere.py) and NO epsilon guard: a zero vector gives 0 / 0 = NaN, not 0. The blend and the norm run in the dtype of the inputs (float32 vectors: float32 norm). Measured: float64 promotion changes the two finite points by at most 4.0e-8; the four antipodal points are discrete inputs (a one-ulp nudge would turn the NaN into a finite vector) and are not perturbed.
